items: intro: A handy reference for common terms...
letter groups A through W, each with term+definition pairs
sections.note: 18 alphabetical letter sections (rc1c2c5..rc1c2c18), ~40 term/definition pairs; mapped as plain headings+paragraphs, not a block

proposed_rules.trigger: A glossary/reference page structured as alphabetical letter groups, each containing multiple term+definition pairs (term as a small heading, definition as a paragraph), with spacer gaps between letters.
proposed_rules.decision: Map each letter as an H2 heading and each term as a bold lead-in/H3 with its definition as the following paragraph, authored as plain default-content in the page body. Do NOT create a dedicated 'glossary' block/table.
proposed_rules.rationale: Chose default-content over a repeating block (the generic repeating-cards-are-one-block pattern) because glossary entries have no card boundaries/background, the list is long (100+ terms) and open-ended, and authors edit definitions far more easily as flowing headings/paragraphs than as rows of a giant one-column block table. Rejected alternative: one 'glossary' block with one row per term.

provenance.evidence: C175 rc1c2c5..rc1c2c18, letters A,B,C,D,F,I,L,M,N,P,R,T,U,W each with 1-6 term/definition pairs

notes: Pure text glossary page; entire body maps cleanly to default-content (headings + paragraphs), no reusable component/block needed.
